ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Law of 13 February 2018, the Law of 25 March 2020 and the Law of 17 December 2021, implementing EU Directives 2015/849, 2018/843 and 2021/1222; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing a Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 22 July 2019 on the operation of the RBE; CSSF Regulation (EU) 2020/425 and CSSF Circulars 18/698 and 19/733; Article 3 of the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies for the registered office obligation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport (historic and current) of every ultimate beneficial owner and authorised signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or competent civil registry of the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs if the issuing country is a 1961 Hague Convention party; otherwise Luxembourg Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Official proof of residential address (e.g., utility bill or municipal extract) of every ultimate beneficial owner and authorised signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal administration or regulated utility provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Luxembourg Consular Legalization on the notarial certification of signature

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter attesting to professional reputation, integrity and source of funds of each founding shareholder or UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed credit institution in the country of residence of the presenter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Luxembourg Consular Legalization after notarization of the signatory bank officer

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, constitutive documents and certificate of good standing of any corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or official trade register of the founder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Luxembourg Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate resolution (extract of minutes) of the corporate founder's board or shareholders authorising the creation of the Luxembourg SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate founder's board of directors or shareholders' meeting, duly notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Luxembourg Consular Legalization on the notarial certification of signatures

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declaration under oath, signed by each UBO and founding party
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The ultimate beneficial owner or founder before a notary or Luxembourg consul
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Luxembourg Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, UBO registration and bank account opening, the appointed compliance officer or external legal counsel must screen all UBOs, directors, managers and authorised signatories against (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, (ii) the OFAC Specifically Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, (iii) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, (iv) the Luxembourg FIU/CRF blacklist and national PEP list, and (v) recognised international PEP and adverse-media databases. Any positive PEP or sanctions flag triggers enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification and senior-management approval. The screening files must be recorded and retained for at least five years after the termination of the business relationship, in accordance with the amended Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers online portal (lbr.lu) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Trade and Companies Register of Luxembourg
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Luxembourg company law (Law of 10 August 1915 as amended), the corporate name may be expressed in any language using Latin characters. If the name is submitted in non-Latin script, for example Chinese characters, an official transliteration into Latin characters must be provided, and only the transliterated spelling is recorded in the RCS. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or to a protected trademark, and must include the legal form indicator 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée', 'S.à r.l.' or 'SARL'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying a public authority, ministerial, municipal or official state institution (e.g., 'state', 'national', 'administrative')
Words indicating banking, insurance, assurance, reinsurance, financial institution or payment institution activity without a licence or prior ministerial approval
Words referring to regulated professions (e.g., 'lawyer', 'auditor', 'notary', 'insurer') without authorisation
Names of existing protected trademarks or notable brands giving rise to a risk of misleading similarity
Terms contrary to public order, morality or mandatory Luxembourg legal provisions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon an RCS name-rejection notice, the founder or the instructing notary may within 15 days submit a reasoned request for reconsideration via the LBR online portal, attaching evidence of distinctiveness and, if applicable, the prior ministerial or regulatory authorisation for the sensitive token. If the registrar maintains the refusal, a formal administrative appeal may be lodged with the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg) by bailiff's writ within two months from notification. The appeal is heard under the rules of the amended Law of 19 December 2008 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and general administrative procedure; it does not suspend the name's unavailability unless urgent provisional relief is granted by the court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as the registered administrative office of a Luxembourg SARL if the address is located in Luxembourg and is operated by a Luxembourg-licensed fiduciary, law firm or other professional service provider capable of receiving correspondence and holding statutory records. However, for a cross-border e-commerce cross-dock and overseas-warehouse business, the virtual office cannot replace operational substance: the SARL must occupy a physical warehouse or cross-dock facility in Luxembourg or, where applicable, establish a fixed establishment elsewhere in the EU. The virtual office may serve as the administrative registered address only; inventory, staff and operational decisions must be traceable to the actual logistics site.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 35% likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 24 months after VAT registration or commencement of warehousing activities. The probability rises to approximately 60% if the SARL holds customs or excise status, maintains material inventory, or shows atypical margins or tax declarations. Inspections may be carried out by the Administration des contributions directes, the Administration de l'enregistrement et des domaines, the Customs and Excise Agency, and the labour inspectorate if staff are employed.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance certificate (certificat de non-conformité) at the Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCS fee schedule for name clearance and reservation, approximately EUR 30

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation and drafting of the articles of association of the SARL, including external legal due diligence review of corporate founder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary office and external Luxembourg corporate law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff plus prevailing market benchmark for corporate legal work, range EUR 2,800 to EUR 4,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration of the deed, statement of commencement and appointment of managers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCS filing tariff, approximately EUR 80 to EUR 100

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation and initial declaration in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official publication tariff fixed by ministerial guidelines, approximately EUR 20

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of the UBO declaration and extract in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory no-fee filing; the notary or appointed manager submits the declaration without charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalisation of six notarised foreign documents (passports, address proof, bank reference, registry extracts, corporate resolution and source-of-wealth declarations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Secretary of State of each origin country and Luxembourg consulates/embassies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular and apostille fees per document, prevailing market benchmark of USD 50 to USD 100 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed fiduciary registered-office and administrative-agent agreement, first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg fiduciary, PFS service provider or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for annual registered office, correspondence collection, AML/CFT reporting and statutory mailing address, EUR 2,500 to EUR 4,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: KYC/AML pre-compliance external legal analysis, UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External compliance counsel in Luxembourg or an international law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for UBO identification, PEP/sanctions screening and compliance file preparation, hourly rates EUR 250 to EUR 400

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation into French, German or English of all non-approved foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-certified translator in Luxembourg or in the origin country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Translator tariff per word/line, prevailing market benchmark approximately EUR 0.25 to EUR 0.50 per word

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account opening and KYC/AML advisory fee, including blocked-capital confirmation for the notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg credit institution and its compliance department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank KYC/account-opening fee, market benchmark; the deposit of minimum share capital itself is not an expense

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales, Articles 710-1 to 710-22 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2007 concernant le registre de commerce et des sociétés; Loi du 1er août 2007 relative aux établissements classés (physical licensing).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), 6-6A Circuit de la Foire Internationale, L-1347 Luxembourg-Kirchberg; online filing portal www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized acte constitutif (articles of incorporation) and notarial certificate of conformity (certificat de conformité) filed with the RCS; publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is EUR 12,000. The full amount must be subscribed and paid up before notarization. Cash contributions must be placed in a blocked escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution and released only after RCS registration. In-kind contributions require a statutory report by an independent réviseur d'entreprises agréé.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF LU SARL. The sole founder, acting as provisional manager, adopts resolutions under the articles and Luxembourg law: 1. Share Subscription: The minimum capital of EUR 12,000 is fully subscribed and deposited in a blocked bank account at a Luxembourg credit institution; release only after RCS registration. 2. Registered Office: Fix the registered office at [Address], Luxembourg City, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, as legal, administrative and tax seat. 3. Officers: Appoint [Manager Name] as sole Gérant and [Alternate] as alternate, each with single signature, to represent the company, open bank accounts, execute filings, and renew permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) through www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a negative certificate search against the RCS index and pending names. Submit a name reservation request or instruct the notary to reserve the corporate name. The selected name must include 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation request
Up to three proposed corporate names
Copy of applicant ID or passport
Confirmation of legal form SARL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, file revised name choices within five working days; the first three amendments incur no additional fee. If the reservation expires, submit a new reservation before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary / Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the notary with the approved corporate name, registered office address, founder and manager details, and evidence of paid-up capital. The notary prepares the articles setting out corporate form, name, duration, object including warehouse and cross-border e-commerce fulfilment services, share capital, management powers, and audit rules. The founders appear before the notary to sign the deed after identity verification.
required_dossiers: Counsel-approved draft articles of association
Founders' passports or national identity documents
Lease or ownership title evidencing the registered office
Current RCS extract of corporate founders, if any
Preliminary declaration of subscription and payment of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or RCS raises statutory objections, amend the provisions by notarial addendum and re-sign before registration; additional notary fees apply only where substantive restructuring of the deed is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Share Capital Deposit and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution regulated by the CSSF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrowed account in the company's name at a Luxembourg bank. Deposit at least EUR 12,000 in cash, instructing the bank to block withdrawals until the notary confirms RCS registration. Obtain a bank certificate of blocked funds addressed to the notary. If in-kind contributions are used, instruct an independent réviseur d'entreprises agréé to issue a contribution report.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Identification documents of managers and signatories
Beneficial owner declaration and corporate structure information
Bank account opening forms and KYC questionnaires
Proof of source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC information, provide certified identity documents and a corporate structure chart. If the deposit is short, top up immediately and obtain a corrected blocked-funds certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) through e-filing by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the notary files the notarized articles, the certificate of conformity dated no more than five days before submission, and the blocked capital certificate using the official e-justice filing procedure. The RCS registers the company, issues the registration certificate, and publishes the deed and related data in the RESA. The company acquires legal personality on registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized original articles of association
Notarial certificate of conformity
Bank certificate of blocked share capital or contribution report
Certified copy of the notary's filing receipt
Initial beneficial owner filing with LBR
Publication request containing corporate name, legal form, registered office, capital and object
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the filing, the notary corrects the dossier within ten working days. If the certificate of conformity is older than five days, obtain a fresh certificate. If the BO declaration is incomplete, supplement the LBR BO register and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Social Security and Operational Licensing Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet.lu, Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), Administration de l'environnement, and ITM
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, file the tax commencement declaration, register for VAT with AEDT, enrol employees with CCSS, and submit the classified establishment authorization or declaration before operating the warehouse. Convene the first board meeting, issue bank mandates, and establish the corporate registers including share register, BO register, minutes, and delegated authorities.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Tax commencement declaration (via Guichet.lu)
VAT registration application
Social security registration and employee declarations
Classified establishment authorization or declaration dossier, including site plan and environmental impact form
Corporate governance register and initial board minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, rely on the Luxembourg grace period for fiscal start declarations. If the environmental permit is not yet issued, restrict operations to non-polluting administrative activities. If fire or workplace inspection identifies deficiencies, implement corrective measures under a compliance order before commencing physical operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction de l'industrie et des services; Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Agency)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'exploitation d'établissement classé (operating authorization for classified establishments) under the Law of 1 August 2007 on classified establishments

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 1 for warehouses above 20,000 m² or storing dangerous goods; Class 2 for facilities between 1,000 m² and 20,000 m²; Class 3 for facilities below 1,000 m² with low-risk operations. Classes 1 and 2 require a full EIA report (étude d'incidences); Class 3 requires registration and a simplified environmental review.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with Luxembourg sewer standards and may not enter surface water without prior treatment. Stormwater must be contained and treated for sediment and hydrocarbons. Disturbance emissions must remain below the thresholds of the Solvent Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU where applicable. Waste handling must follow Luxembourg waste law with segregation of hazardous materials. Noise levels at residential façades must not exceed night-time limits of 35–40 dB(A) unless adequately mitigated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Compagnie Grand-Ducale des Sapeurs-Pompiers (CGDIS) or a recognized fire engineering service; structural load inspection by a licensed engineer for racking, mezzanines and heavy storage; workplace clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering emergency routes, occupational safety, equipment integrity and staff welfare facilities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg has a unitary national tax administration: (1) Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) - competent for VAT registration, e-TVA filings, indirect tax audits, and customs liaison; (2) Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - competent for corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC), net wealth tax (IF), and individual income tax; (3) Administration des douanes et accises (ADDA) - competent for customs export/import procedures and excise. Official electronic portals: MyGuichet.lu (business portal), guichet.lu (legal information), ACD eCDF e-filing portal, AEDT e-TVA portal, and Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) e-Registration for RCS filings. No sub-national tax distinctions apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Luxembourg SARL: (1) Incorporate by notarial deed and register the SARL with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the LBR e-Registration platform; registration with the RCS creates the company's matricule number and automatically triggers opening of the corporate tax file with the ACD, which assigns the national tax identification number (numéro d'identification). (2) File the RCS incorporation confirmation and register the beneficial owner in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE). (3) Before commencing taxable activity, submit form 640 (Déclaration d'assujettissement à la TVA) to the AEDT to obtain the Luxembourg VAT number in the format LU + 8 digits (e.g. LU26375215); issuance typically takes 2-3 weeks with no registration fee. (4) For a non-resident foreign entity selling directly into Luxembourg without an establishment: register directly with the AEDT (no turnover threshold for local taxable supplies subject to Luxembourg VAT); a non-EU supplier must appoint an AEDT-approved fiscal representative (représentant responsable). (5) Use the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) portal for distance sales of goods to EU consumers below the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold and for B2C telecommunications/broadcasting/electronic services. (6) Note: separate foreign-direct-investment screening under the Luxembourg FDI law may apply to non-EU shareholders, but it is not a tax precondition. The foreign parent does not require a Luxembourg TIN if the SARL is the taxable operator; a notarized power of attorney should be granted to the local tax representative/manager.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a resident SARL (siège statutaire in Luxembourg) is a corporate tax subject fully taxable at entity level on worldwide income; no pass-through treatment is available for a SARL under Luxembourg domestic law. Corporate income tax (IRC) applies at a flat 17% on taxable income above EUR 200,000 (with reduced graduated brackets for profits up to EUR 200,000); a 7% solidarity surcharge applies on the IRC; municipal business tax (ICC) applies at approximately 6.75% in Luxembourg City, yielding a combined effective income tax burden of approximately 24.94%; net wealth tax (IF) applies at 0.5%. Worldwide scope applies to residents, mitigated by the participation exemption (Article 166 LIR) for qualifying dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings of at least 10% held for 12 months; non-resident companies are taxed only on Luxembourg-source income. No tax-exempt zone applies to the Luxembourg SARL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg law does not provide a domestic check-the-box or general fiscal-transparency election; a SARL is mandatorily taxed as a corporation. Available elections: (a) Fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR - a Luxembourg-resident company or Luxembourg branch of an EEA company holding at least 95% of the SARL may elect to consolidate the SARL's taxable results for IRC/ICC purposes (minimum 5-year commitment); (b) VAT grouping (unité TVA) under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law - the SARL and linked Luxembourg-established entities with financial, economic, and organisational links may file as a single VAT taxpayer with one VAT number; (c) US federal tax classification election - the SARL (or its US parent) may file IRS Form 8832 to treat the SARL as a disregarded entity or partnership for US federal tax purposes only, with no Luxembourg law effect; (d) Hybrid mismatch rules (Article 168ter LIR, ATAD implementation) disallow deductions for hybrid mismatch arrangements and are mandatory, not elective; (e) The SARL may elect to apply the participation exemption rather than the underlying-tax credit method and may opt into the Luxembourg IP box regime (Article 50bis LIR) providing an 80% exemption on qualifying IP income derived from nexus-eligible assets.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT known as TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 transposing EU Directive 2006/112/EC, administered by the AEDT. Rate structure effective 1 January 2025: standard rate 17% (increased from 16%); intermediate rate 14% (e.g. wines, certain fuels); reduced rate 8%; super-reduced rate 3% on approved basic goods. Reverse charge applies to B2B cross-border services, imported goods, and certain domestic supplies; no sales and use tax or GST regime exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR (euro). Luxembourg has no de minimis turnover threshold for establishment-based registration: any Luxembourg-established SARL carrying out taxable supply of goods or services must register for VAT from its first taxable transaction; simplified annual filing is available only where annual turnover is below EUR 30,000. For non-established sellers: no registration threshold applies to B2B supplies subject to reverse charge or to Luxembourg-consumer supplies requiring local VAT; the EU-wide distance-selling threshold is EUR 10,000 in total cross-border B2C distance sales of goods, above which Luxembourg VAT registration becomes mandatory (the exporter may instead register in each destination member state or use OSS); B2C TBE services require registration in Luxembourg without any threshold unless declared through the non-union OSS scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory B2B e-invoicing mandate and no real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or digital tax certification regime applies in Luxembourg as of 2025. B2G mandate: invoices issued to Luxembourg public-sector entities must be transmitted as structured e-invoices (PEPPOL/UBL format) through the national e-invoicing platform; phased B2G enforcement was completed in 2023. VAT returns, recapitulative statements, and periodic payments are filed electronically through the AEDT e-TVA portal (monthly for turnover above EUR 2 million, quarterly for EUR 30,000-2 million, annual for below EUR 30,000). Customs export and import declarations are lodged electronically with the ADDA via the EU Export Control System (ECS) and COVID/ICS2 systems; no separate tax clearance or stamping certificate is required for export consignments. The EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) package is expected to introduce EU-wide structured e-invoicing and transaction-level digital reporting for cross-border B2B supplies by 2030; Luxembourg transposition is pending and should be monitored for the cross-dock 3PL operating model.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 56 of the Luxembourg VAT Law (EU Article 146(1)(a)): supplies of goods dispatched or transported by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf to a destination outside the EU are exempt with credit (0% rate) provided the goods physically leave EU territory within 90 days of supply and the supplier retains contemporaneous transport evidence. Article 57: intra-EU B2B dispatch of goods is zero-rated where the customer supplies a valid EU VAT ID (VIES-validated), the goods are dispatched within 90 days, and the supplier files the recapitulative statement (EC Sales List) and, where applicable, Intrastat declarations. Cross-dock 3PL services (storage, handling, picking, packing, and reloading at the Luxembourg fulfillment hub) directly connected with the export of goods to a third country are zero-rated under Article 58 (EU Article 146(1)(e)) where the logistics contract, customs status of the goods, and warehouse records demonstrate the export destination. Input VAT refunds: the Luxembourg SARL deducts input VAT on its periodic e-TVA return; a non-EU client may reclaim Luxembourg input VAT under the 13th Directive refund procedure through the AEDT with application by 30 June of the year following the charge year, while EU-established claimants use the portal of their own member state with statutory deadline of 30 September.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / electronic export declaration lodged via the EU ECS through the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration - ADDA)

Transport evidence: Bill of Lading (sea), Air Waybill (air), CMR consignment note (road), or CIM rail consignment note showing departure from the Luxembourg cross-dock hub and arrival at a destination outside the EU
Commercial invoice and packing list cross-referenced to the export declaration, sales order, and fulfillment contract
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT MT103 confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the overseas buyer
Proof of third-country status of the consignee (invoice address outside the EU, destination-country customs entry or import VAT payment evidence, or destination customs release record)
Warehouse movement and custody records (WMS pick/pack/load logs, stock-in-transit reports) for the ISIC 5210 / NAICS 493110 cross-dock 3PL hub
EC Sales List (recapitulative statement) and Intrastat declarations for intra-EU dispatches zero-rated under Article 57 where the customer is an EU VAT-registered business
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT and ADDA may audit VAT and customs positions within the general 5-year limitation period (extended to 10 years where VAT fraud or intentional evasion is established). Where the export zero-rating is not substantiated - in particular where the 90-day physical dispatch rule is not met or the SAD/BL/warehouse documentation is inconsistent - the supply is re-characterized as taxable in Luxembourg at the standard 17% rate (effective 1 January 2025) with retrospective clawback of the differential VAT for all related consignments, plus statutory late-payment interest (indexed annually, approximately 7.8%-7.9% per annum) and administrative penalties under Articles 65-68 of the VAT Law: a 10% augmentation for documentary negligence, fines generally from EUR 1,000 to EUR 10,000, and for intentional evasion an administrative fine of up to 100% of the tax evaded; criminal prosecution under the Luxembourg Criminal Code may add imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years and director disqualification. Fraudulent export schemes (fictitious goods, forged SAD/BL, shell consignees, circular transport) trigger joint and several liability of the SARL, its managers, and the 3PL warehouse operator, and the zero-rating is clawed back with full retroactivity plus interest. Luxembourg has no exchange controls and the BCL imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day proceeds-realization convention used in this compliance pipeline serves as the documentary audit benchmark - proceeds received materially later than 180 days invite transfer-pricing, VAT-benefit, and commercial-reality scrutiny and may result in reclassification of the supply as taxable at 17%.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as prudential and AML/CFT supervisor, the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance for financial-sector policy, and the European Central Bank (ECB) as the currency authority within the Eurosystem.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Luxembourg. No exchange-control regime restricts current-account or capital-account transactions; the free movement of capital is guaranteed by TFEU Article 63 and EU Directive 88/361/EEC. Profit remittance by an SARL requires an ordinary shareholders' resolution and satisfaction of the Luxembourg net-asset maintenance test (minimum legal capital of EUR 12,000 maintained); no exchange-control approval is required. Outbound dividends attract a 15% domestic withholding tax, reducible under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or an applicable double tax treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation quota for export proceeds. The 3PL fulfillment entity may retain receivables in EUR, USD, or any freely chosen currency in multi-currency accounts, subject only to standard corporate reporting, transfer-pricing documentation, and annual financial-statement disclosure obligations under Luxembourg tax law.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High for operational liquidity. PSD2-authorised Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions passporting into Luxembourg (e.g., Airwallex, Currenxie, PPRO) provide multi-currency settlement, local-ACH collection, and lower-cost FX conversion for the e-commerce fulfillment cash cycle. Legal constraints: such EMIs are not credit institutions under the Luxembourg law of 5 April 1993; they cannot issue the notarially recognised capital-blockage certificate (certificat de blocage de fonds) required by the Luxembourg notary for the SARL's EUR 12,000 paid-up capital, and escrow or large-balance treasury roles are generally reserved to CSSF-licensed credit institutions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Pure remote onboarding is not statutorily prohibited; CSSF AML/CFT rules (Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02) require identity verification by reliable, independent means. In practical bank policy, tier-1 Luxembourg banks usually require at least one in-person or video-interview KYC session with the legal representative and each UBO holding 25% or more; an alternative is a notarised power of attorney enabling a Luxembourg-resident professional (lawyer, notary, or auditor) to attend, combined with consular or apostilled identity documents. The final onboarding tier remains subject to each bank's internal KYC committee discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate UBO structure with intermediate holding companies and opaque ownership layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Unexpired certified passports or national IDs of all natural-person UBOs and directors; full corporate-chain organizational chart; RCSL (Luxembourg Register of Commerce) extracts and certificates of incorporation for each intermediate entity; Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) extract; notarised source-of-funds documentation (share purchase agreements, bank references); and a written source-of-wealth narrative for the ultimate shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity third-party settlement flows from cross-border platform marketplaces (Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, etc.) into the operational account, causing volatile turnover that may be misread as layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed fulfillment-services master agreements with each platform and marketplace; six to twelve months of platform payout statements and reconciliation reports; the ISIC 5210 cross-dock/warehouse operating model memo; a 12-month cash-flow forecast; pro-forma commercial invoices; and a documented AML risk self-assessment classifying the activity as Low_Risk_Standard under CSSF guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound disbursements to foreign warehouse sub-contractors, customs brokers, and 3PL carriers in non-EU jurisdictions (e.g., China, Hong Kong, United States).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete commercial contracts with each counterparty (warehousing, transport, customs brokerage agreements); tax residency certificates and business-licence evidence for counterparties; an economic-substance file proving Luxembourg substance (board minutes, premises lease, payroll lists); the shareholder resolution authorising the treasury policy; and a transfer-pricing policy documenting arm's-length fees for cross-docking and last-mile logistics services.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The SARL's EUR 12,000 minimum capital must be fully paid up via a SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer from the subscriber to a blocked account (compte séquestre) opened at a Luxembourg credit institution in the name of the company in formation; the notary's attestation confirms the blockage, and funds are released upon RCSL registration. Recommended purpose codes: 'CAPITAL' or ISO 20022 'G100' for capital contributions; the remitter name must exactly match the subscriber named in the articles of association, and the bank may request the shareholders' subscription resolution and pro-forma incorporation deeds. Additional shareholder loans or capital increases follow the same purpose-code logic with a board resolution attached.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR disbursements flow via SEPA Credit Transfer through the Luxembourg Interbank Clearing (LIPS-GI) or TARGET2; cross-border non-EUR payments use SWIFT MT103 with appropriate transaction-type codes; supplier settlements above exposure caps may be structured as documentary collections or irrevocable commercial letters of credit subject to UCP 600 for high-value warehouse equipment and logistics contracts. The treasury stack may connect a local Luxembourg IBAN with Airwallex or banking APIs to automate ACH-native collection from US marketplace settlement accounts and convert to EUR at the point of funding via spot or forward lines.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/CNH out-right FX forwards and FX swaps
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing currencies with underlying non-convertibility exposure
Currency swaps (fixed/fixed and fixed/floating) with licensed Luxembourg credit institutions
Plain-vanilla FX call/put options (premium-based) for contingent USD and CNH cash flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registered company details (dépôt annuel / confirmation annuelle) with payment of the yearly RCS fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), filed via MyGuichet e-file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year; due on or before 31 December of the year following the registration anniversary for every RCS-registered SARL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of EUR 37.50 per automatic reminder; unresolved annual confirmation default exposes the SARL to blocking of RCS certificates and enforced removal from the trade register (radiation d'office) with judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts publication (dépôt légal des comptes annuels): balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes, and management report approved by the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must approve the annual accounts within 6 months of the balance sheet date (by 30 June for a calendar-year SARL); approved accounts must be filed within 1 month of approval, i.e. no later than 31 July for calendar-year entities (7 months from year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Publication default triggers court fines under the 2002 register law (EUR 100–2,500 per breached filing obligation); recurring non-publication leads to refusal of RCS certificates, radiation d'office, and director liability for resulting damages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting minutes, shareholder resolutions (discharge of management, appropriation of result), and updated corporate minute book retained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records at the registered office; available for inspection by LBR, notaries, the statutory auditor, and tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual meeting held within 6 months of the financial year-end; minutes must evidence approval of accounts and all decisions taken in the relevant calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct filing fee; absence of valid AGM minutes invalidates the annual accounts approval chain and exposes managers and auditors to liability and court-ordered convening proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO annual confirmation and beneficial ownership update (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs – RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation of UBO data accuracy bundled with the RCS annual confirmation; any change in beneficial ownership or shareholding structure must be declared within 30 days of the reporting entity becoming aware of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Wilful non-declaration of UBO information is criminally sanctionable (fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years); administrative blocking of the company file and RCS certificates until the declaration is regularized.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and municipal business tax return (déclaration d'impôt commercial communal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year SARL: filing due by 31 December of the year following the taxable period (e.g. FY 2024 filed by 31 December 2025); where a tax notice is issued, the filing deadline is 31 May of the assessment year, extendable to the following 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the assessed tax; late-payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month; continued non-filing after a formal reminder allows ex officio taxation and criminal proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (déclaration de l'impôt sur la fortune) and payment of the annual minimum net wealth tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 May of the assessment year following the tax year; extendable to 31 December of the same assessment year through the tax advisor when no tax notice has been issued
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing is penalized by ex officio assessment, a late-filing fine, and monthly interest of 0.6% on the net wealth tax due; the minimum net wealth tax of EUR 535 remains payable even for dormant SARLs.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé applies when the SARL exceeds two of the three small-company criteria for two consecutive financial years: (i) balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million; (ii) net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; (iii) average workforce above 50 employees. Audit may also be required by the articles of association, by shareholders representing 10% of the share capital, or by applicable consolidated group requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan comptable normalisé and the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies as amended); IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for statutory accounts and is mandatory for SARLs forming part of listed EU groups preparing consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every direct or indirect holder of 25% or more of the share capital, voting rights, or economic interest must be recorded in the RBE. The annual RCS confirmation movement requires re-certification of the beneficial ownership data as at the confirmation date; any share transfer or ownership change must be declared within 30 days of knowledge, and the manager or registered agent must correct the register upon any annual discrepancy.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – 3,500 per annum (EUR 1,100 – 3,200) for professional Luxembourg registered-office domiciliation, filing agent, and corporate secretarial services; mid-market range EUR 1,500 – 2,500 for a small cross-border 3PL SARL.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 – 16,000 for a full statutory audit by an approved réviseur d'entreprises agréé; not applicable to a SARL that remains below the small-company exemption thresholds, where no certified audit fee is incurred unless the articles of association or shareholder requisition require an auditor.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), investment tax credit (up to 8% of qualifying investments), participation exemption for dividends and capital gains (100% exemption under conditions)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and Form 600 (Municipal Business Tax Return) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu or the Luxembourg tax administration's e-filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after the end of the fiscal year (extendable to 6 months upon written request)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification (name, address, RCS number, fiscal year)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg tax identification number and permanent establishment details if applicable
Report Luxembourg-source income attributable to the permanent establishment
Only expenses directly related to Luxembourg PE are deductible; maintain supporting documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and incentives (IP box, investment tax credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only if eligible under Luxembourg law; attach detailed schedules
Ensure transfer pricing adjustments are reflected; attach TP documentation if required

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of EUR 250 to EUR 2,500, plus 0.6% per month interest on unpaid tax; additional penalties for inaccurate returns up to 10% of underpaid tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must obtain a tax residence certificate (TRC) from their home jurisdiction and submit it along with a completed Form 22 (or 22bis) to the Luxembourg paying agent before the dividend distribution. The payer must withhold at the reduced treaty rate if the conditions are met; otherwise, the excess can be reclaimed via a refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory, 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive (if beneficial owner is an EU affiliate holding at least 25% for 2 years); Interest: 15% statutory, 0% under the same directive for qualifying EU companies; treaty rates may further reduce to 0-10% depending on the jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50 million group turnover for Master File; EUR 1 million intercompany transactions for Local File
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) requiring entities to have adequate office, employees, and management in Luxembourg. For a 3PL cross-dock operation, operational substance is inherent, but documentation must evidence real activity, decision-making, and risk management in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of taxable income, overstating deductions, or falsifying records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to 100% of evaded tax, plus interest at 0.6% per month; criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Lack of economic substance, no real business activity, or artificial arrangements to avoid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of income, penalties up to 10% of assets, and potential liquidation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil restitution, fines, and criminal charges for facilitating tax avoidance; travel bans and imprisonment up to 3 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement anti-money laundering procedures, inadequate customer due diligence, or failure to report suspicious transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 1 million, license revocation, and mandatory compliance audits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally fined and imprisoned up to 5 years for AML violations; civil liability for damages
